verify_fix docstring | low | Claim that 'daedalus.spine.docref_gate' establishes text gone from document. Uncheckable. | Verify docref_gate module code.
resolve_reference docstring | low | Claim about absent-module case: 'daedalus.nemesis', 'daedalus.cerberus', 'daedalus.root' examples. Uncheckable. | Verify the tree and actual references.

handoff.purpose: Complete resolve_reference, define _rel_key, scan, check_denominator, verify_fix_counts, verify_fix, verify_fixes.

symbols.name: resolve_reference
symbols.note: Resolves a reference against the module tree. Returns Reference with state resolving/broken/skipped.

symbols.name: _rel_key
symbols.note: Normalises a repo-relative path as Reference records it.

symbols.name: scan
symbols.note: Measures the whole prose corpus against the tree. Returns DocRefReport.

symbols.name: check_denominator
symbols.note: Checks denominator: resolving_after < resolving_before returns evidence_destroyed FixVerdict, else None.

symbols.name: verify_fix_counts
symbols.note: Verifies fix using before count and after report.

symbols.name: verify_fix
symbols.note: Verifies fix using before and after reports.

symbols.name: verify_fixes
symbols.note: Judges a whole document's findings under one denominator check.

claims.text: The denominator half, on its own. ``None`` means the denominator HELD.
claims.why: Function returns None when resolving_after >= resolving_before.

claims.text: Every path that judges a prose fix goes through here first, because :func:`verify_fix_counts` calls it on its first line and there is no other way in.
claims.why: verify_fix_counts calls check_denominator on its first line.

claims.text: It takes counts, not reports, because the count is all the rule needs.
claims.why: Chunk does not contain caller code; function indeed takes counts.

claims.text: ORDER IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY. The denominator is checked FIRST.
claims.why: verify_fix calls verify_fix_counts which calls check_denominator first.

claims.text: Taking the document out withdraws the claim AND lowers ``resolving`` in one move, so a check that asked "is the claim gone?" first would call that a success and reward exactly the behaviour the island metric already taught this repo to expect.
claims.why: Logic: if claim removed, resolving count drops. Denominator check catches that.

claims.text: Both honest remedies pass: naming the symbol that exists now (``fixed``) and withdrawing the stale claim (``claim_withdrawn``). Neither lowers the count of references that resolve.
claims.why: verify_fix_counts returns fixed or claim_withdrawn; both require denominator not destroyed.

claims.text: ``claim_withdrawn`` is the verdict for a key found in neither list, and that reading is only sound when the target was taken from ``before.broken``: then absence really does mean the sentence went.
claims.why: Chunk does not verify target origin; function assumes caller correctness.

claims.text: A caller that reconstructs a target from somewhere else -- a command line, a serialised and TRUNCATED copy in a queue's evidence -- can produce a key that never matched anything, and will be told the claim was honourably withdrawn. Such a caller must establish independently that the claim was there to withdraw; :mod:`daedalus.spine.docref_gate` does it by requiring the text to be gone from the document.
claims.why: Refers to external module daedalus.spine.docref_gate not in chunk.

claims.text: The denominator is a property of the corpus, not of any one reference, so it is asked once and asked FIRST: if the evidence was destroyed, that is the only verdict returned and no per-reference verdict is manufactured to sit beside it looking reassuring.
claims.why: Function first calls check_denominator; if destroyed returns only that verdict.

claims.text: NO EMPTY GREEN. An empty ``targets`` returns ``False``. Verifying nothing is not the same as verifying something and finding it sound, and a gate that passed on zero targets would turn "we lost the findings" into a green tick -- which is the exact shape of failure the rest of this harness exists to refuse.
claims.why: Returns (bool(verdicts) and all(v.ok for v in verdicts), verdicts). Empty targets gives verdicts=(), bool(()) is False.

claims.text: The MODULE tree is read from ``repo_root`` on both sides. That is deliberate: the denominator compares two prose snapshots against ONE tree, so a difference in ``resolving`` is attributable to the prose edit and to nothing else. It is not a general time machine and must not be used as one.
claims.why: Chunk does not show how scan is called; function reads from root each call.

claims.text: An override may ADD a document the snapshot on disk no longer has -- the deletion case, which is the one the denominator exists to catch.
claims.why: Code adds overrides not in seen to planned.

claims.text: absent in this snapshot: not scanned, not an error
claims.why: Code: if text is None: continue.

observations.what: resolve_reference uses classes dict from cache; if head not in classes or modules, returns broken. If head in classes but chain length >=2 and member not in classes[head], returns broken. Otherwise resolving.
scan function handles overrides: if text is None, file is skipped (not scanned, not error).
verify_fixes returns False for empty targets, preventing false positive.
